name: Korean 10-step skincare routine (K-beauty routine)

card.summary: A layered K-beauty regimen of double cleansing, toning, essences, serums, moisturiser and sunscreen aimed at a hydrated, luminous complexion.
card.aka: K-beauty routine; Korean skincare routine; glass skin routine
card.note: Each step is optional; routines are adjusted to individual skin, and some ingredients can irritate.

quick.overview:
The Korean 10-step skincare routine is a layered regimen from South Korean K-beauty. It combines a double cleanse with toners, essences, serums, sheet masks, moisturiser and daytime sunscreen, with the aim of a hydrated, luminous complexion often called glass skin, rather than heavy foundation.

The routine averages about 10 steps, though it is adjusted for skin type, hormonal changes and lifestyle. Its spread is credited to the Korean Wave, celebrity endorsements and a 2014 drama that boosted a brand's sales.
quick.how: Wikipedia describes the typical sequence as a double cleanse, sheet masks, essences, lotions, serums, moisturisers and daytime SPF, with a thicker sleep cream replacing sunscreen at night. Users add or drop steps to suit skin concerns.
quick.risks: Layering many products raises the number of ingredients on the skin, and ingredients such as botanical extracts or snail mucin can irritate some people. Wikipedia notes that claims about natural ingredients need better sourcing. Sunscreen is part of the daytime routine.

lead: The Korean 10-step skincare routine is a multi-stage regimen associated with K-beauty, the umbrella term for South Korean skincare products. It typically includes a double cleanse, sheet masks, essences, lotions, serums, moisturisers and daytime SPF, with a sleep cream at night in place of sunscreen. [1]

Its appearance goal is a hydrated, luminous complexion, often called glass skin, achieved with skincare rather than layers of makeup. It spread through the Korean Wave (Hallyu), celebrity endorsements and a 2014 drama that boosted sales of a featured brand. [1]
The number ten is an average rather than a rule, and routines are adjusted for factors such as hormonal changes and lifestyle. [1]

chain: Skin barrier kept hydrated, daytime sun protection
angle.text: Followers use the sequence to keep skin clean, hydrated and protected from the sun, aiming at a glowing, even look without heavy makeup.

infobox: Double cleanse, toner, essence, serum, sheet mask, moisturiser, SPF

paras: The routine layers several product types. The day sequence ends with SPF, while at night a thick sleep cream replaces sunscreen. Products often use botanicals such as green tea, orchid and soybean, and unusual ingredients such as snail slime, bee venom, starfish extract and pig collagen. [1]

Wikipedia traces Korean beauty practices to the Three Kingdoms period, with the Goryeo era seen as a peak and fair skin signalling status in the Joseon dynasty. Modern popularity is credited to Hallyu, celebrity endorsements, a 2014 drama, duty-free shopping and tourism. South Korea is described as a hub for skincare research, development and manufacturing. [1]

Beauty standards in Korea can pressure people and affect self-esteem, and the Escape the Corset movement has pushed back on rigid standards. Claims about natural ingredients are flagged as needing citations. [1]
No studies found on the 10-step routine as a whole.

timeline.event: A Korean drama boosts sales of a featured brand, an early marker of K-beauty's international rise. [1]
